text: The man will likely prevail because when he acquired both properties five years ago, the recorded easement was extinguished by merger since one person could not hold an easement over their own land. Upon selling only the house to the purchaser two years later, no new easement was created or reserved in the warranty deed, so the right-of-way did not revive automatically. Therefore, the man is entitled to block access as he owns both the dominant and servient estates again. CONFIDENCE: 95
